en: Udāna 1.8 Saṅgāmajisutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Saṅgāmaji had arrived at Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One.
The former wife of the Venerable Saṅgāmaji heard:
“Venerable Saṅgāmaji has reportedly arrived at Sāvatthī.
Taking her child, she went to Jeta’s Grove.
At that time, the Venerable Saṅgāmaji was sitting at the foot of a certain tree for his midday rest.
Then the former wife of the Venerable Saṅgāmaji approached the Venerable Saṅgāmaji; having approached, she said this to the Venerable Saṅgāmaji:
"Support your young son, ascetic.
When this was said, the Venerable Saṅgāmaji remained silent.
A second time, the former wife said this to the Venerable Saṅgāmaji:
“Support your little son, ascetic!
A second time, the Venerable Saṅgāmaji remained silent.
A third time, the former wife said this to the Venerable Saṅgāmaji:
“Support your little son, ascetic!
A third time, the Venerable Saṅgāmaji remained silent.
Then the former wife of the Venerable Saṅgāmajī placed that boy before the Venerable Saṅgāmajī and departed, saying:
"This is your son, ascetic; support him.
Thereupon, the Venerable Saṅgāmajī neither looked at the boy nor spoke to him.
Then the venerable Saṅgāmajī’s former wife, having gone not far away, looked back and saw the venerable Saṅgāmajī neither looking at nor speaking to that boy. Having seen this, it occurred to her:
“This ascetic has no need even for a son.
Thereupon, she turned back, took the boy, and departed.
With the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, the Blessed One saw such a misfortune befall the former wife of the Venerable Saṅgāmaji.
Then, having understood this matter, on that occasion the Blessed One uttered this inspired exclamation:
“One does not rejoice in what is coming.”
He does not grieve when departing;
him who has conquered the battle and is freed from attachments,
him I call a brahmin.
The eighth.
